- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) in recent days, model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after recent spikes (e.g., 60+), especially if sentiment was neutral or negative prior — adjust upward by 2–5% for such periods.  
- Model often lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending strongly.  
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — if price is above 60 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates final 5–7 days; apply a small upward bias (1–3%) to end of forecast if sentiment is positive.  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to adjust — trigger a mid-horizon correction upward.
